title: Garry Tan on YC's structure, resilience and community: Out of Office walk through SF
summary: Garry Tan walks through San Francisco with Michael McNano and explains why YC dropped its continuity fund to focus on one core business, why rejection is part of the founder test, and why venture should be bigger and less clubby. He also covers how he got into local politics and why community building matters.

principles.text: Being rejected is a normal first step; founders face constant rejection, so treat it as a resilience test.
principles.quote: the first step to getting into YC is getting rejected from YC.

principles.text: Founders get rejected at every turn (users, investors, hires, commenters), so build tolerance early.
principles.quote: you're going to be rejected in countless ways as a founder at every turn at every turn of the journey.

principles.text: Take pro rata to keep owning decacorns, since most returns come from a few huge outliers and dilution kills them.
principles.quote: just taking the paradas means you never miss the decacorns and you know how the power law works

principles.text: Stay a lifelong partner to portfolio companies: no formal end to support after the program.
principles.quote: Make us earn it. Come back. Like do office hours with us.

principles.text: Treat YC like a two-sided marketplace where investors are scarce supply and founders are near-limitless demand.
principles.quote: the limiting reagent for Airbnb is actually hosts

principles.text: Early-stage investors should avoid herd syndicates and show up before a company is obvious.
principles.quote: Show up, do early stage, you know, fun people before it's obvious.
